## 1. Idea and references

**The idea in one sentence.** In the weeks when the weekly three-index switch (Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100 supertrends) is OUT **and** the weekly MAUc1 gold supertrend is SELL — the **OUT-SELL regime** — holding **the liquid ETF plus each of the three indices whose own supertrend SIGN is still BUY, in equal parts** (variant `-idx`: no BUY index → 100% liquid ETF; one → 50% liquid ETF, 50% that index; two → one third each), instead of the original sleeve, changes what the three-index switch earns: its CAGR and its worst fall; tried on both base sleeves (50/50 = T06/T11 Part A, 80/20 = T08/T11 Part B) on the two windows where the switch has been tested on the real parents.

**Where it came from.** Manu, chat 2026-11-25: "if you understood this, then I want you to make one more test, T15, where, when the 3-switch, 3-index switch, and Gold both are in sell, you will buy Liquid Bees as well as the direct index, which is in buy. If there are 2 indices available, then you will do 33%, 33%, 33%, 33% so that it's some 200 between the liquid and the 2 indices that aren't by. If there is 1, then you do 50-50 between liquid and the index that is in buy." Claude restated it (thirds summing to 100; at most two indices can be BUY in an OUT week, since three BUY is IN) and asked five questions. His answers: (1) no index BUY in an OUT-SELL week → 100% liquid: "yes correct"; (2) "direct index" = the index level itself, price return, filled at OHLC4 as T09, and "Liquid Bees" = the LBES cash series: "yes, direct index"; (3) both base sleeves and both windows as T14: "yes"; (4) when the BUY set changes inside the regime: "when new index become buy you should buy that index too, applying a rebalance"; (5) nulls and chance checks: "No need for null tests and chance check". **Claude's reading of answer 4, stated in chat and not objected to** (decision point D3, default taken on Manu's go-ahead): the symmetric case is the same — **an index that turns SELL inside the regime is sold and the rest re-equalised**. His "lets execute the T15" (chat 2026-11-25) approved the plan and, with it, the defaults of its decision points D1–D3 (§2).

**The decision this will change.** What the book should hold in the OUT-SELL regime: the original sleeve (50/50 or 20% GOLDBEES / 80% cash), half parent + half GOLDBEES (T14 `-half`), the liquid ETF alone (T14 `-liq`), or the liquid ETF plus the BUY indices (`-idx`). The answer is **descriptive**: what each choice earned over the same weeks, prices and costs, as differences from the other holdings, with the spell-by-spell ledger. **No statement about chance or skill is made.** A pass of a comparison is at most PROVISIONAL: the variant was proposed after seeing the results of the original rule and of T14 on both windows.

**What is already known.**

| Ref | What it says | Relationship |
|---|---|---|
| T06 (COMPLETE 2026-11-06), F-AA-S07 | Fixed 50/50 sleeve, 2019-01-02 → 2026-10-22: switch beats random in-or-out timing (CAGR percentiles 97.4, 94.1, 96.8, 94.6 against N4.10) | `50-orig` on W2 is this rule |
| T08 (COMPLETE 2026-11-12) | Same switch, sleeve 80/20 GOLDBEES/cash when MAUc1 BUY, 20/80 when SELL: equity timing PASS (97.2, 94.2, 97.0, 95.0), gold timing FAIL | `80-orig` on W2 is this rule; **seen** |
| T11 (COMPLETE 2026-11-17) | Both rules on the rebuilt real parents, 2014-09-01 → 2019-01-02: all six criteria FAIL, low power | `50-orig` / `80-orig` on W1; **seen** |
| T13 (COMPLETE 2026-11-18) | T11 with a 2-of-3 entry: all six FAIL; a post-hoc variant on a seen window | precedent for a post-hoc variant |
| **T14** (COMPLETE 2026-11-23) | The OUT-SELL regime held half parent + half GOLDBEES (`-half`) or 100% liquid (`-liq`): `-half` beat its original in every book (+3.3 to +5.8 pp CAGR W1, +2.0 to +4.7 pp W2), not established as timing; `-liq` lowered CAGR in 16 of 16 book-windows (-0.04 to -1.79 pp) | **T15's direct parent**: same regime, third holding. In the OUT-SELL weeks with no BUY index, `-idx` **is** `-liq`; so `-idx` minus `-liq` isolates what holding the BUY indices adds, `-idx` minus `-orig` is the whole change |
| F-AA-M02 (T03) | A script that edits a document holding a frozen section must prove it did not change it | `fill_writeup.py` must leave §1–§3 byte-identical |

**What this test is NOT asking.**
- Whether holding the BUY indices beats **chance** or whether the three index signals pick the right indices: no null is run (waiver); the results say what each holding earned over these weeks, nothing about whether the BUY indices were chosen well.
- Whether any rule beats holding the parent (a comparator), or whether another weighting or signal would do better. Eight rules, no search.
- Whether the variant has skill on weeks nobody has seen. There are none.
- Whether a real index fund or ETF would have earned what the price index did (§3, contaminants).
- Whether the best of the eight rules is the one to trade: picking it from these tables is a selection on seen data (§2).
- Whether the rebuilt 2014-2018 parent NAV is the published one (none exists before 2019-01-02).

## 2. Hypothesis and pre-registered comparisons

**Written before any run, 2026-11-25.** What was already known:
- **Both windows are seen, and so is T14.** T06, T08, T11, T13 and T14 ran rules on these weeks, and T14's per-book results, its regime ledger (which spells gained, what the parent, GOLDBEES and cash returned in each) and its finding that `-liq` lost CAGR in every book-window were seen before the request. In particular the W2 spell of 2021-01-29, which holds Midcap 100 + Smallcap 100 for all 10 weeks under `-idx`, is the spell where the parent rose 20.6% and T14's `-half` gained most. **The variant was proposed after seeing all of this**: any finding is **PROVISIONAL at most**, and there is no hold-out (signals after 2026-10-30 are not approved).
- **No null is run** (Manu's waiver, 2026-11-25, as T10's). **No statement about chance or skill can be made.**
- **The regime and B were counted before this section was written** (`spell_counts.py`, `logs/step_1_spell_counts.json`; signals, calendars and basket dates only; no price, NAV or return): **W1** (D26 calendar): 228 weekly decisions, first state IN; IN 93, OUT-BUY 81, OUT-SELL 54 weeks in 8 spells; in the OUT-SELL weeks **k = 0 in 21, k = 1 in 18, k = 2 in 15**; weeks holding at least one index **33, in 6 of the 8 spells**; B changes inside OUT-SELL 8 (each traded). **W2** (D17-extended calendar): 410 decisions (409 for SCMO_0007), first state OUT-BUY; IN 201, OUT-BUY 163, OUT-SELL 46 in 8 spells; **k = 0 in 24, k = 1 in 2, k = 2 in 20**; weeks holding an index **22, in 6 of 8 spells, 10 of them one stretch (2021-01-29)**; B changes 6. Trades per rule from regime, gold and B changes: W1 `50-orig` 15, `-half` and `-liq` 24, `50-idx` and `80-idx` 32 (80-orig 24); W2 `50-orig` 18, 80-orig/-half/-liq 27, `-idx` 33. R3 windows: W1 from 2015-01-02: 44 OUT-SELL weeks, 23 holding an index (k0/k1/k2 21/14/9); W2 live from 2021-11-01: 31 OUT-SELL weeks, **9 holding an index** in 3 spells (k0/k1/k2 22/1/8).
- **The effective sample is the index-holding stretches: 6 spells per window**; in W2 one stretch (2021-01-29, 10 weeks) is 10 of the 22 index weeks. Every write-up says so.
- **Settled by Manu's go-ahead, 2026-11-25 (the plan's decision points, defaults taken):** **D1** what is judged: the four descriptive comparisons C1-C4 below, pass mark 3 of 4 books (the D-table and the ledger are printed in any case); **D2** the six T14 rules (`-orig`, `-liq`, `-half` on both bases) are re-run by the same engine as comparators and as the regression gate against T14's stored NAVs; **D3** an index that turns SELL inside the regime is sold and the rest re-equalised to 1/(k+1). Manu may overrule any before the engine runs; a change after the freeze is a revision beside this file, never an edit.
- **Expectation, declared, no direction claimed.** In the 21 (W1) and 24 (W2) weeks with no BUY index `-idx` equals `-liq`; the whole difference from `-liq` comes from the 33 / 22 index weeks. From `-orig`, `-idx` also drops all GOLDBEES in the regime, which cost `-liq` -0.04 to -1.79 pp in T14. The index leg earns the index's price return (no dividends, no fund cost): a real fund would differ.

### 2.1 The eight rules

Regimes are read at each weekly decision: **IN** = all three index SIGNs BUY; **OUT-BUY** = switch OUT and MAUc1 SIGN BUY; **OUT-SELL** = switch OUT and MAUc1 SIGN SELL. In OUT-SELL let **B** be the set of indices whose own D03 SIGN is BUY at that decision (0, 1 or 2 of Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100) and k = |B|. A target is the book's split across parent / GOLDBEES / cash / each index; T14's `(e, gw)` maps to parent e, GOLDBEES (1−e)·gw, cash (1−e)·(1−gw), indices 0.

| Rule id | Base | IN | OUT-BUY | **OUT-SELL** | Is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `50-orig` | 50/50 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | T06 / T11 A (comparator, regression) |
| `50-liq` | 50/50 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | cash 1 | T14 variant (comparator, regression) |
| `50-half` | 50/50 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | parent 0.5, GOLDBEES 0.5 | T14 variant (comparator, regression) |
| **`50-idx`** | 50/50 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | **cash 1/(k+1), each index in B 1/(k+1)** | **new** |
| `80-orig` | 80/20 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2 | GOLDBEES 0.2, cash 0.8 | T08 / T11 B (comparator, regression) |
| `80-liq` | 80/20 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2 | cash 1 | T14 (comparator, regression) |
| `80-half` | 80/20 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2 | parent 0.5, GOLDBEES 0.5 | T14 (comparator, regression) |
| **`80-idx`** | 80/20 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2 | **cash 1/(k+1), each index in B 1/(k+1)** | **new** |

So in OUT-SELL: k = 0 → 100% cash; k = 1 → 50% cash, 50% that index; k = 2 → 1/3 cash, 1/3 each of the two indices. `-idx` holds no parent and no GOLDBEES in the regime. **Change one thing at a time:** the only change from T14's rules is the OUT-SELL target.

### 2.2 Execution of the new states

Everything not listed is T14 §3 unchanged (decide on the last session of each ISO week and T0; read the latest D03 and MAUc1 rows dated on or before the decision; trade on the next session at OHLC4; 10.4 bps a side on every value traded, 20.8 bps round trip primary, 0 and 50 as robustness; initial position free; the last decision is made, not traded).

1. **When a trade happens.** On the session after decision j iff decision j's target differs from decision j−1's. For `-idx` the target includes B, so **a change of B inside OUT-SELL is a trade** (Manu's answer 4), as is every entry into and exit from the regime. A change of an index SIGN while IN or OUT-BUY does not trade (those targets do not depend on B). The six T14 rules use T14's trigger unchanged.
2. **What a trade does.** The existing `trade()` generalised to index lines: at the session's fill prices (stocks OHLC4, GOLDBEES de-spiked OHLC4, cash at its level, **each index at its own OHLC4**), V = value of all holdings; target value of each line = target share × V; traded = Σ|target − held| over every line (stocks, GOLDBEES, cash, each index); cost = traded × cost_bps ÷ 2 ÷ 1e4; every target is scaled by (V − cost) ÷ V. **A change of B re-equalises every line** (cash included) to 1/(k+1): Midcap 100 + Smallcap 100 → Midcap 100 sells all Smallcap 100 and moves Midcap 100 and cash to 1/2 each; Smallcap 100 → Midcap 100 + Smallcap 100 buys Midcap 100 to 1/3 and trims Smallcap 100 and cash to 1/3 each.
3. **No reset inside an unchanged target.** While B and the regime are unchanged, weights drift and nothing is traded weekly.
4. **Parent rebalances while `-idx` is in OUT-SELL:** the parent share is 0, nothing is traded (as e = 0 in T14). The `-half` comparators keep T14's D1 rule.
5. **Index NAV marking.** Units × the index close. On a calendar session with no index bar (W2: the Budget weekend sessions 2020-02-01, 2025-02-01, 2026-02-01, all last sessions of their ISO week, so decision sessions, never trade sessions) the last close is carried and counted in `audit.json`. If a trade session ever lacks an index bar, the engine stops (asserted).
6. **Same-session collisions** (as T14): a basket change on the session of a regime trade is one trade to the new basket at the new target; a gold flip and an exit on the same decision is one trade straight to the new target; a B change and an exit on the same decision is one exit trade.

### 2.3 The pre-registered comparisons (descriptive; no null)

For each window w in {W1, W2} and base b in {50, 80}, judged per book after 20.8 bps over the whole window:

| # | Statement about `b-idx` | Comparator | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | earns more than the original rule | `b-orig` | CAGR higher in ≥ 3 of 4 books |
| C2 | its worst fall is no deeper than the original's | `b-orig` | maximum drawdown shallower or equal in ≥ 3 of 4 books |
| C3 | holding the BUY indices adds to holding only cash in the regime | `b-liq` | CAGR higher in ≥ 3 of 4 books |
| C4 | does better than holding half the parent and half GOLDBEES in the regime | `b-half` | CAGR higher in ≥ 3 of 4 books |

**16 comparisons** (4 × 2 bases × 2 windows). "Higher" and "shallower or equal" are by the unrounded statistics. Printed beside each: the difference in pp per book, Calmar, volatility, trades and cost paid. **The four books are one market seen four times**, and in OUT-SELL weeks `-idx` holds exactly the same indices and cash in every book, so their agreement is close to automatic and "3 of 4" is weaker here than in earlier tests. **A pass is a description of seen weeks, never a claim about chance.** Choosing the best of the eight rules from these tables is a selection on seen data, and the write-up says so. No multiplicity adjustment is made (nothing is tested against chance).

### 2.4 The headline the decision needs (descriptive)

- **D-table:** per window, book and cost: CAGR, maximum drawdown, Calmar, volatility of every rule, and the differences `-idx` − `-orig`, `-idx` − `-liq`, `-idx` − `-half`; start and end dates; trades and cost; weeks and sessions in each regime and in each k.
- **Regime ledger:** for each OUT-SELL spell and each B stretch inside it: dates, weeks, B, the return of each index, cash, GOLDBEES and the parent over the stretch (first fill to last fill), and each rule's return over it, so the reader sees which stretches carry the difference.
- **Comparators** (benchmarks): hold the parent; hold each index alone over the window; the **constant mix** at `-idx`'s own average shares of parent, GOLDBEES, cash and each index (mean over the weekly decisions of the rule's target shares), rebalanced at every decision, which shows how much of a difference is just a different average exposure.

### 2.5 Outcome map (frozen)

| Pattern (per window, per base) | Conclusion |
|---|---|
| C1 and C3 pass | holding the BUY indices with cash earned more than the original sleeve and more than cash alone on this window; PROVISIONAL (seen, post-hoc, no null) |
| C3 passes, C1 fails | the indices beat cash but giving up GOLDBEES cost more than they added |
| C3 fails | holding the BUY indices did not beat cash in the regime on this window |
| C4 passes / fails | `-idx` did better / worse than T14's `-half` on this window |
| R4 flips a passing comparison when one spell is left out | the result rests on that spell; say which; at most a description of it |
| the two windows disagree | report both; no general statement; the 2019-2026 window is the one the live product traded |
| R3 (live) disagrees with the full window | reported in the verdict and status note |
| a V gate fails | nothing is read; fix; new run directory |

### 2.6 Validity gates (any failure: nothing below may be read)

| # | Gate | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | Independent verifier `analysis/verify_t15.py`, written by a **different agent** from the engine's, from `logs/verifier_spec.md`, never opening `t15_engine.py` (it may read `verify_t14.py`) | Imports nothing from the engine, `approved_data.py` or any AA analysis module; parses `APPROVED_DATA.md` itself; checks every input is APPROVED with matching sha256 and a through-date covering the window. Re-derives from the raw files, per window: the decisions, regimes and B; the eight rules' NAVs at every cost and R1-R5 variant; every trade (regime entries and exits, B changes, sleeve and basket trades). End NAV within relative 1e-9, daily NAV within 1e-9. Exits 0 only if rows were compared and none failed; corrupted copies must exit non-zero (a B week flipped, a B change not traded, an index leg at 1/2 where k = 2, a `-idx` regime week holding GOLDBEES, a NAV scaled, a trade removed, an index price shifted by one session) |
| V2 | Point in time | every decision reads Master and MAUc1 rows dated on or before it; every trade is on a later session; counted; violations 0 of a count > 0 |
| V3 | Index data tie | at every weekly decision of both windows, D03's `Index` column equals the index close of D25 / D25c on that date for all three indices (ties the traded prices to the signals); every trade session has a bar for each index traded |
| V4 | Regression and identities | (a) the six T14 rules reproduce T14's stored `daily_nav.csv` (every book, cost, rule, both windows) and `trades.csv` to relative 1e-12; (b) with every index price replaced by the cash level and cost 0, `-idx` equals `-liq` to 1e-12; (c) `-idx` equals `-liq` on every session before the first trade into an index; (d) automated diff of shared functions against `t14_engine.py` lists only the expected changes; (e) the signals equal the SIGN columns of D03, D24 (W2), D24b (W1) at every decision; (f) one-instrument always-in identity, as T14 |
| V5 | Trade and cost identities | after every `-idx` trade into or inside OUT-SELL, each index in B and cash = 1/(k+1) of the value after cost, parent and GOLDBEES 0, to 1e-12 of NAV; index units 0 outside OUT-SELL; all units constant between trades; cost = traded × cost_bps ÷ 2 ÷ 1e4; one entry with k = 2, one B change and one exit worked by hand in §4.0a |

Oracle, negative-control and planted-effect controls (N6.7) are **not run**; they are untested (§6).

### 2.7 Robustness (reported; they set a finding's status, not the comparisons)

- **R1:** C1-C4 and the D-table at 0 and 50 bps.
- **R2:** C1-C4 and the D-table with LIQUIDCASE as the cash leg (W1 the whole window; W2 from 2024-01-24, as T08/T14). Cash is 1/3 to 100% of `-idx`'s regime holding, so this matters.
- **R3:** C1-C4 and the D-table on W1 from 2015-01-02 and on W2's live decisions from 2021-11-01 (each with its own first state, as T14). W2's live window has 9 index weeks in 3 spells.
- **R4: leave one spell out.** For each OUT-SELL spell s, a run in which `-idx` holds `-liq`'s target (100% cash) during spell s only; C1-C4 recomputed. Shows whether one spell (in W2, 2021-01-29) carries the verdict. Deterministic.
- **R5: fund-cost drag on the index leg.** C1-C4 with each index's price series replaced by an adjusted series whose daily return is the index's minus 0.5 pp ÷ 252 (an expense and tracking drag), i.e. every index OHLC4 and close of session i multiplied by (1 − 0.005 ÷ 252)^i, i counted in sessions of the window's calendar from T0. The opposite side, dividends, is **not run**: no approved dividend series exists; disclosed as untested.

## 3. Methodology

**Data.** Every file is a row of `data/APPROVED_DATA.md` (status APPROVED) and is opened only through the approved-data check; the engine writes `inputs.csv` (path, through-date, bytes, sha256, approved row, usable-from) from those rows and stops on a sha256 mismatch or a read before a usable-from date. **Each window uses exactly the inputs and conventions of T14** (so the six T14 rules reproduce T14's stored results, gate V4(a)) **plus the daily index prices**:

| | **W1** (T11's / T14's window) | **W2** (T08's / T14's window) |
|---|---|---|
| Dates | 2014-09-01 → 2019-01-02 | 2019-01-02 (SCMO_0007: 2019-01-04) → 2026-10-30 |
| Calendar | D26 NSE sessions (`index_daily_pre2019/nse_trading_days.csv`, 1,070 sessions) | D17 dates of the EXTENDED published NAVs (`extended_2026-11-06/published_nav/SCMO_<p>.csv`, 1,932 sessions) |
| Stock OHLC (D18), Polyplex correction (F-AA-D14), basket weights (D19), skips and dates (D05) | `data/holdings_matrix/SCMO_<p>_ohlc.csv`, `price_corrections.csv`, `*_holding_weight_matrix.csv`, `_columns.csv`, `_holding_weight_sources.csv`; `Historical Data/frozen_2026-09-25/Rebalance_history/` | same |
| Parent | rebuilt from baskets and D18 prices, as T11 | the same rebuild, as T08 |
| Three-index signals (D03) | `extended_2026-10-30/Master/Master_{Nifty100,MC100,SC100}.xlsx` (SC100 rows dated 2011-11-25 or later) | same |
| MAUc1 signal | D24b `extended_2026-11-12/MAUc1_from_2003/Master_MAUc1.xlsx` | D24 `extended_2026-11-06/MAUc1/Master_MAUc1.xlsx` |
| GOLDBEES (D09), de-spike range | `analysis/cache/why_gold_ohlc_eikon_extended_2026-11-04.parquet`; range: D24b's daily file, as T11 | same parquet; range D12 (to 2026-09-28; raw OHLC4 after it), as T08 |
| Cash (D11) / R2 | `LBES_Adjusted_Price_data_extended_2026-11-05.csv` / `liquidEtfFinal_extended_2026-11-05.csv` | same |
| **Index prices (new)** | **D25** `Historical Data/extended_2026-11-12/index_daily_pre2019/{Nifty100,MC100,SC100}_daily_ohlcv.csv` (`guard_window` with 2014-09-01 for SC100) | **D25c** `Historical Data/extended_2026-11-25/index_daily_2019_2026/{Nifty100,MC100,SC100}_daily_ohlcv.csv` |
| R3 | start 2015-01-02 | live decisions from 2021-11-01 |
| R2 | LIQUIDCASE as cash, whole window | LIQUIDCASE from 2024-01-24 |

No draws are made, so no seeds are used.

**Test evidence read by gates only (not data):** `tests/T14/evidence/headline/{w1,w2}/{daily_nav.csv, trades.csv, decisions.csv}`. Not read: D09b, D03b, the tag files D20–D23, D15 AA books, any PENDING or SUPERSEDED row, T14's `draws.csv`. Reading T14's stored files is a regression gate, not an input to any T15 number.

**Construction, in order.** Steps 1–3, 5, 7–9 and the unchanged parts of 4 and 6 are T14 §3 (and, through it, T11 §3 for W1 and T08 §3 for W2).

1. **Calendar** and **decision dates** per window as above: T0, then the last session of each ISO week after T0; the decision on the last session of the window is made but not traded.
2. **Signals at decision date d.** The latest Master row of each of the three indices and of MAUc1 dated on or before d. IN iff all three SIGN are BUY. g = BUY iff the MAUc1 SIGN is BUY. Regime: IN, OUT-BUY, OUT-SELL as §2.1. **B** = the indices (in the order Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100) whose own SIGN is BUY at d; used only in OUT-SELL by `-idx`.
3. **Targets**: one function `targets(rule, in, g, B)` returns the split parent / GOLDBEES / cash / each index. For the six T14 rules it returns exactly T14's `(e, gw)` mapping, so their path is unchanged. IN: the parent's basket in force at its listed weights renormalised to 1.
4. **Trades.** As §2.2. A trade is due on the next session after decision j (j ≥ 1, a session exists) iff the target vector differs from decision j−1's (for the six T14 rules T14's trigger `e[j] != e[j−1] or (e[j] < 1 and gw[j] != gw[j−1])`; for `-idx` any change of regime or, in OUT-SELL, of B).
5. **No reset inside an unchanged target.**
6. **Parent rebalances.** A basket takes effect on the first session on or after its `availableDate`. While IN the old basket is sold and the new bought at that session's OHLC4. While `e = 0` (including `-idx` in OUT-SELL) nothing is traded. While `e = 0.5` (the `-half` comparators) T14's D1 rule: only the stock part is re-weighted, GOLDBEES and cash untouched.
7. **Initial position** at T0's close, no cost, in every realisation: the target of the decision at T0, with NAV 1 (an IN start holds the basket in force at T0 as drifted since its availableDate; an OUT start holds its sleeve; an OUT-SELL start of `-idx` holds cash and each index of B in equal parts at that day's closes. The two full windows do not start there (W1 starts IN, W2 OUT-BUY), **but both R3 windows do** (Step 1: W1 from 2015-01-02 and W2-live from 2021-11-01 start with the switch OUT and gold SELL), so in R3 `-idx` starts in OUT-SELL with the B of that day, `-half` as T14 (half the drifted basket plus half GOLDBEES), `-liq` all cash).
8. **NAV, statistics:** cash account + Σ units × close (stocks, GOLDBEES, each index); years = (sessions − 1) ÷ 252; CAGR = NAV_end^(1/years) − 1; maximum drawdown, Ulcer index, days ≥ 10% below the running peak, longest time under water, volatility = SD of daily returns × √252, Calmar = CAGR ÷ |maximum drawdown|.
9. **Comparisons** as §2.3, from the stored NAVs; the comparators of §2.4 by the same engine.

**How the test works, in plain words.**

- **The series.** The book is one of the four real parents. Every Friday three weekly index signals and gold's own weekly signal are read. If all three index signals say BUY, the book holds the parent's basket. Otherwise it is in a "sleeve" and the original rule says what the sleeve is: half GOLDBEES and half cash (50/50), or 80% GOLDBEES and 20% cash when gold is BUY and 20/80 when gold is SELL (80/20). T15 changes only the weeks when the three-index signal is OUT and gold is SELL: there the book holds the liquid ETF together with each index that is still on BUY, in equal parts, the index itself bought at its own average of open, high, low and close with no dividends and no fund cost. Every price and level comes from the approved files of the table above; the 2014-2018 parent is rebuilt from the parent's baskets and stock prices as in T11 (no published NAV exists to check it). *[each series' first and last value printed in §4.0a]*
- **One decision.** On a Friday, look up the latest row of the three index files and of the gold file. Work out the regime (IN, OUT-BUY or OUT-SELL); in OUT-SELL list which of the three indices say BUY; read off the target for each of the eight rules, and if it differs from last Friday's the trade is on the next session at the average of open, high, low and close. *[one real row printed in §4.0a: a k = 2 week]*
- **The result of one path.** Units of each stock, GOLDBEES, cash and index are fixed between trades; each day the NAV is the sum of units × price; CAGR and drawdown come from that NAV. *[printed in §4.0a]*
- **A change of the BUY set.** If, while the book is in this regime, a second index turns BUY, the book buys it and the liquid ETF and the first index are trimmed so the three lines are one third each; if an index turns SELL it is sold and the rest are made equal. Each such change costs the usual 10.4 bps on the value traded. *[an entry with k = 2, a B change and an exit worked by hand in §4.0a]*
- **The comparisons.** The new rule's CAGR and worst fall are placed beside the same book's CAGR and worst fall under the original rule, under T14's liquid-ETF-only rule and under T14's half-parent rule, on the same weeks, prices and costs. No random weeks are drawn, so no percentile or p-value exists; a "pass" means the difference had the stated sign in three of the four books.
- **Leave one spell out and the fund-cost drag.** R4 re-runs the new rule with one OUT-SELL spell held in cash only, to see whether that spell carries the result; R5 re-runs it with half a percentage point a year taken off each index.
- **The comparators.** Holding the parent is what the book would do with no rule; each index alone is what the index leg earned; the constant mix holds the rule's own average shares all the time and shows how much of any gain is just a different average exposure.

**Point-in-time rule.** A decision at d reads Master rows dated at or before d only; a trade is on a session after d. The engine asserts both for every decision, counts them, and writes the counts to `audit.json` (V2). The Master rows were produced afterwards by the production code and are not signals traded at the time, and no MAUc1 row was traded by the desk; disclosed, not corrected.

**Execution and cost.** AGENT.md R1 (next-session OHLC4, price return, 10.4 bps a side, weights drift between rebalances); the first position at T0 is free; no sale at the end; a stock bar without open, high or low is filled at the close; the GOLDBEES fill is T03's de-spike; every regime trade, B change and parent rebalance pays on the value traded, the index lines included. An index is filled at its own OHLC4 from D25 / D25c.

**Effective sample size and power.** 6 index-holding spells per window (the independent unit for the change; 5 and 3 in the R3 windows' W1 and W2-live), 8 OUT-SELL spells; 228 and 410 weekly decisions; the four books share one market, so they are one sample seen four times. No MDE: no test statistic is computed.

**What the comparisons control for, and what they do not.** Nothing is controlled for chance (no null). They say what each holding earned over the same weeks. In the weeks with k = 0 `-idx` and `-liq` are the same book, so C3 is decided entirely by the index-holding weeks; C1 and C4 also reflect that `-idx` holds no GOLDBEES and no parent in the regime.

**Known contaminants** (T14's §3 list, copied, plus the index leg):

| Contaminant | Handling |
|---|---|
| W1: no published NAV exists before 2019-01-02, so the rebuilt 2014-2018 parent cannot be checked | Disclosed; the rebuilt NAV is written beside the results with a caption saying so |
| W1: nine manual Eikon exports (`data/missing_rics/`, provenance unrecorded, F-AA-D01) supply bars for delisted stocks held in this window | Disclosed (affects the parent and so `-orig`, `-half`, not `-idx` in OUT-SELL) |
| Price returns only (dividends not credited on stocks, GOLDBEES, **or the index leg**) | Disclosed. **The index leg is a price index with no dividends and no fund cost, not a tradable instrument**: a real index fund or ETF would differ by roughly the dividend yield minus its costs, and Smallcap 100 / Midcap 100 funds were thin or absent in 2014-2019; R5 tests the cost side only |
| The index prices come from production's Refinitiv file with no second source | Tied to the signals by D25c's checks and V3 |
| W1: the session 2017-10-19 (Muhurat evening) is in D26 and has D25 bars but no D18 bars; GOLDBEES has no bar on 2016-10-30 | T11's last-close stand-in and previous-close fill, counted |
| W2: three Budget weekend sessions (2020-02-01, 2025-02-01, 2026-02-01) have no index bar | Last close carried, counted; they are decision sessions only |
| W2: GOLDBEES fills after 2026-09-28 use the raw OHLC4 (no D12 range) | As T08; counted in `audit.json` |
| The cash file's source before 2026-08-10 is unrecorded (F-AA-D09); the extension runs about 0.5 pp/yr rich against LIQUIDBEES; ~2 days of weekend accrual counted twice (≤ 0.02%) | Disclosed; R2. **Cash is 1/3 to all of `-idx`'s regime holding**, so this contaminant matters here |
| The rule, its weights, the MAUc1 signal and now the variant were chosen after seeing 2014–2026 results | Disclosed (§2). There is no unseen stretch |
| The four books share one market, one in-or-out series and one gold series, and in OUT-SELL weeks `-idx` holds identical indices and cash in all four | Not independent; "3 of 4" is a consistency check |
| Master rows (indices and MAUc1) are a backfill by the production code; MAUc1 is a futures series with roll artifacts | Disclosed |
| `check_approved_data.py` lists `Historical Data/extended_2026-11-12/SOURCE.md` as unregistered (exit code 0) | Not read by this test |
